Your opportunity
  
  
This is a business-facing engineering role. You will sit with business users, work out what is slowing them down, and turn those problems into AI and data solutions that reach production. The work starts with a conversation at someone’s desk, not a ticket in a queue.
  
  
Janus Henderson is undertaking a firm-wide AI transformation to become the most technologically sophisticated asset manager in the industry. Our AI capability sits in a single centralised function under the Head of AI, and Forward Deployed Engineering is the part of it that embeds with the business and builds what business units cannot stand up alone. You will work alongside the AI Enablement Partners, who surface and triage demand: where they establish what a team needs, you build it. Reporting to the Principal Forward Deployed Engineer, you own your solutions from first conversation to live running.
  
  
The work spans the full stack — sourcing internal and external data, curating it into views that answer the questions a desk actually asks, and making it reusable through Accio, our centralised MCP server. The most advanced work is investment engineering: building quantitative capability on Nexus, our agentic workspace, and taking it from one desk to a firm-wide offering such as relative-value signal generation. Your toolkit spans Python and SQL, LLMs and agent frameworks, MCP, Azure AI Foundry through the AI Team’s model gateway, Snowflake, and Azure with Terraform, Docker, and CI/CD.
  
  
What success looks like
  
  

* You ship. What you build reaches production, is used by the business unit you built it for, and stays healthy once live.
* Business users come to you early enough that you shape the problem rather than receive finished requirements.
* Capability proven on one desk is exposed through Accio and Nexus so other teams consume it rather than rebuild it.
* You need less direction over time, taking on engagements that are less defined and more technically demanding.

**Embed with the business**

* Sit with business users — portfolio managers, analysts, traders, marketing, sales, HR, and operations — to understand their workflows, their data, and their day-to-day friction.

* Design, build, and productionise bespoke, higher-complexity AI solutions, owning them through to live running.
* Prototype with the business close at hand, then harden what works into production rather than leaving a demonstration.
* Own the architecture and design decisions for your solutions, keeping them secure, scalable, and aligned to the enterprise core stack.
* Take solutions through evaluation, observability, and our AI governance checkpoints, and keep them healthy afterwards.

* Build advanced investment capability on Nexus and make it available across the firm.
* Work with quantitative researchers and investment teams to take models and signals from one desk into a supported, firm-wide capability.
* Put validation, monitoring, and reproducibility around signal output investment professionals rely on, and help take citizen developer workflows through to production.

* Source data through APIs, vendor feeds, and enterprise systems, and build the ingestion pipelines that keep it flowing.
* Curate raw data into business-focused views, and own its lineage, quality, and freshness.

Job Title: Software Engineer
  
  
**About The Company**
Palantir Technologies builds software platforms that help organizations integrate, analyze, and act on complex data. Its products support customers across commercial industries and government, helping teams address consequential challenges in areas such as healthcare, energy, manufacturing, finance, and public services. Palantir’s work brings together software engineering, data integration, analytics, and operational workflows so users can make informed decisions and put insights into practice. The company’s environment is collaborative and mission-oriented, with teams working closely across disciplines and with customers to understand real-world problems.
  
  
**About The Role**
As a Software Engineer at Palantir, you will design, develop, and maintain software that helps customers work with complex data and improve important operational processes. You will contribute across the software development lifecycle, from understanding user needs and exploring technical approaches to implementing, testing, and supporting production-ready solutions. The role combines strong engineering fundamentals with practical problem-solving. You will work with engineers, product leaders, designers, deployment specialists, and customers to turn challenging requirements into dependable, usable software. The specific projects and technologies may vary based on team needs and customer context.
  
  
**Qualifications**
We are looking for candidates with a strong foundation in computer science, software engineering, or a related discipline, gained through professional experience, academic study, or equivalent practical work. You should be comfortable programming in at least one modern language and able to learn new tools and systems as needed. A thoughtful approach to algorithms, data structures, testing, debugging, and system design is important. Successful candidates communicate clearly, collaborate constructively, and can explain technical decisions to people with different backgrounds. You should be curious about how software is used in practice, attentive to reliability and security, and willing to take ownership of problems from investigation through delivery. Experience building production systems, working with databases or distributed services, or developing user-facing applications is helpful, but not required for every team.
  
  
**Responsibilities**
Design, implement, review, and maintain software that meets functional, performance, reliability, and security requirements. Work with colleagues and customers to clarify problems, gather feedback, and translate user needs into practical technical plans. Build and improve services, applications, integrations, and data workflows, selecting appropriate designs and tools for each problem. Write readable, testable code and contribute to automated testing, documentation, and engineering standards. Investigate defects and operational issues, identify root causes, and deliver improvements that reduce recurring problems. Participate in design reviews and technical discussions, communicate progress and trade-offs, and coordinate work across teams. Support software in production by monitoring behavior, responding to issues, and incorporating lessons learned into future development. Contribute to a respectful team culture through knowledge sharing, thoughtful feedback, and dependable collaboration.

Employees may also have access to resources that support physical and mental wellness. Details vary by employment location and individual circumstances and will be shared during the hiring process. The role provides opportunities to work on complex technical challenges, collaborate with experienced colleagues, and see how software can support real-world decisions and operations.
